rows.note:
Added by G17. `filesystem-read` is a new value in this campaign's effect vocabulary — the five that existed were none, inbound-socket, outbound-socket, subprocess and filesystem-write, and none of them describes a route that reads a directory it was told about. The requirement itself is not new work: M19 and M30 both shipped against it and the campaign had no row for it, so the feature had no denominator and no case could have failed on it. Reach limit, stated rather than buried: the route serves only servers declaring a package directory and 0 of the 21 upstreams on this machine declare one (M30, planning/evidence/M30-reach.txt), so every case citing this requirement is measured against a CONSTRUCTED server.

RECONCILED 2026-08-27. This row was allocated REQ-026 by G17 and G19 at the same time, off the same `main`. G19's REQ-026 keeps the number and states the WIRE contract: what GET /servers/:name/document serves and the exact refusal each rule names. This row keeps the half G19's does not carry -- that those documents are DRAWN in the Mac capability document panel, that a figure resolves from inside the package and nothing else is fetched, and that each refusal identifies itself on screen. Its cases are the swiftui lane's (CASE-0185..0190, CASE-0194) and they need a requirement to trace to; folding them into a router-daemon requirement would put a panel assertion inside a route's contract. G17's one WIRE case, CASE-0184, traces to REQ-026 instead, because that is the requirement its assertion is of. The two rows overlap on 'read out of the declared package directory' deliberately: neither text was rewritten, so the overlap is visible rather than resolved by editing delivered work. The `filesystem-read` effect class is left exactly as G17 declared it and is NOT in campaign.py's closed EFFECT_CLASSES -- `check` has flagged that since G17 landed and still does; G19's REQ-026 note records the same gap from the other side, having declined to name a class the vocabulary does not hold. Reconciling the vocabulary is the campaign owner's, not this renumber's.
